deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a copied excerpt, probably in Riemann's hand, from a review printed in the Heidelberger Jahrbücher der Literatur, 1860. The review discusses O. F. Allihn's article 'Über das Leben und die Schriften J. F. Herbart's nebst einer Zusammenstellung der Literatur seiner Schule', published in the Zeitschrift für exacte Philosophie, ed. Allihn and Ziller, Bd. I, H. 1, pp. 44–99.

The excerpt covers four points:
(1) Sources for Herbart's biography: articles in the Allgemeine Preussische Staatszeitung and the Augsburger Allgemeine Zeitung; Voigt, 'Zur Erinnerung an Herbart' (Königsberg 1841); a further item published by Hartenstein, Hamburg 1853; and above all G. Hartenstein's introduction to Bd. I of Herbart's Kleine philosophische Schriften, pp. V–CXX (Leipzig 1842).
(2) Herbart's intellectual development. His critique of Schelling's Fichtean-period youthful writings ('Über die Möglichkeit einer Form der Philosophie', 'Vom Ich') gave the first occasion for his growing break with Fichte's system (S. 58). A quotation follows on the demand for strict scientific rigour, which must test whether the foundations are really sound.
(3) The bibliography of Herbart's writings, following the order of the collected edition, and of writings about Herbart.
(4) A long roster of Herbartians: Drobisch, Griepenkerl, Exner, Brzoska, Hartenstein, Strümpell, Taute, Lott, Waitz, Volkmann, Thilo, Lazarus, Steinthal, R. Zimmermann, Allihn, Ziller and others. Two further names, one illegible plus Lotze, are said to have a related orientation. The review concludes that this proves the growing spread of the Herbartian school.

The context is Riemann's documented interest in Herbart's philosophy and psychology. The next folio excerpts Herbart Werke I p. 507 on the origin of spatial representation. There is no derivation to reconstruct.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a bibliographic and biographical excerpt about Herbart's school, with no mathematical content. Riemann's engagement with Herbart (his remark 'Ich bin Herbartianer' and his philosophical fragments) is well known and documented in the Nachlass and in Weber–Dedekind's edition.
transcription_corrections: The phrase '... in Fichte'schen Geiste geschriebenen Jugendschriften "über die Möglichkeit einer Form der Philosophie" und ...' refers to Schelling's early writings. It should read roughly: 'Herbart's [Urtheil] über Schelling's in Fichte'schem Geiste geschriebene Jugendschriften "Über die Möglichkeit einer Form der Philosophie" und "vom Ich"'.
'Unter den Vertretern der Schule werden ... in Breslau (+ 1838)' is likely 'Unterholzner in Breslau (+1838)'.
'Voigt, ... in Wien' is likely 'Voigt, Lott in Wien' (F. K. Lott).
'Thilo, ... zu ...' is likely 'Thilo, Superintendent zu Markoldendorf im Hannöverschen'.
The heading likely reads 'Heidelberger Jahrbüchern 1860, 7. [crossed out] u. 8ten Heft gegebenen Anzeige' rather than 'Neunten Heft'; uncertain.
The duplicated 'Hartenstein, Hartenstein [?] in Leipzig' probably contains a second, different name (e.g. 'Bartenstein'); uncertain.
